berlin.note: Extensive U-Bahn, S-Bahn, tram and bus network.

paris.note: Dense Metro network with over 300 stations city-wide.

london.note: The Underground plus extensive bus and rail coverage.

tokyo.note: One of the world's busiest and most extensive metro/rail systems.

new york.note: 24/7 subway system covering most of the city.

amsterdam.note: Trams, metro and one of the best cycling infrastructures in the world.

vienna.note: U-Bahn, tram and bus network rated among Europe's best.

hong kong.note: MTR metro system reaches almost the entire territory.

singapore.note: MRT metro network with high reliability.

madrid.note: One of the largest metro networks in Europe.

prague.note: Compact metro plus tram network covers the city well.

copenhagen.note: Metro, S-train and strong cycling culture.

rome.note: Smaller metro network than other European capitals; buses fill gaps.

lisbon.note: Metro, trams and funiculars cover the hilly city centre.

istanbul.note: Growing metro network plus extensive ferries across the Bosphorus.

dubai.note: Modern but limited-coverage metro; a car is often still useful.

tehran.note: Metro network covers much of the city, supplemented by BRT bus lines.

tabriz.note: A smaller metro network supplements buses; less coverage than Tehran.

cairo.note: Africa's oldest metro system, but coverage is limited relative to the city's size.

los angeles.note: Historically car-dependent; rail network is expanding but still limited.
